business_summary.text: Lloyds Enterprises Limited is a diversified holding platform spanning steel and allied products trading, real estate through Lloyds Realty Developers, and strategic investments including Lloyds Engineering Works, Geomysore and a 4.13% stake in Lloyds Metals & Energy.

call_points.text: LEWL delivered a record quarter with consolidated income of ₹540.2 Cr, up 139%, and net profit of ₹68.2 Cr, up 127%.
The SISCOL acquisition of 17.98% for ~₹219 Cr takes LEWL's combined structural fabrication capacity to 150,000 MTPA.
Geomysore began commercial operations at Jonnagiri on 24 June 2026, targeting around 400 kg of gold in FY27 and scaling towards a tonne a year.
The demerger scheme has NSE and BSE approval; NCLT approval is pending.
Shareholders will receive 1 Lloyds Realty share for every 2 Lloyds Enterprises shares under the demerger.
SISCOL had FY26 revenue of ₹816.87 Cr, net profit of ₹43.42 Cr and an order book of about ₹1,134 Cr.
LEL holds a ~31% economic stake in Geomysore through its 50% interest in Prakar Estate and Promoters LLP.
LEL holds a 4.13% stake in Lloyds Metals & Energy, giving exposure to an integrated iron ore and steel franchise.
No numeric FY27 revenue, margin or capex guidance is given; the presentation is a portfolio overview.
LEWL secured orders exceeding ₹50 Cr for Eco Pickling Surface (EPS Gen-4) steel surface treatment technology.
Real estate MoUs cover over 270 acres across MMR, with revenue potential exceeding ₹5,000 Cr.
The restructuring will merge LRDL and Indrajit Properties into LEL, then separate real estate into a separately listed Lloyds Realty Limited, subject to approvals.
LRDL follows an asset-light model with negligible debt and JV-led development.
LEL holds a ~31% stake in GMSI, acquired in Q2FY26 for ₹200 Cr.

operating_notes.text: Standalone other income of ₹348.89 Cr in FY26 included profit on sale of investments of ₹183.71 Cr and income from sale of rights of ₹129.19 Cr.
The company sold 3,42,54,299 shares of subsidiary Lloyds Engineering Works during FY26.
Subsidiary Lloyds Realty Developers entered an MOU to acquire 51% of Calculus Logistech for ₹60 Cr, with a further ₹242 Cr commitment.
LEWL order book exceeds ~₹8,335 Cr as of FY26, split infrastructure ₹5,692 Cr, engineering ₹2,493 Cr and electrical ₹151 Cr.
GMSI's Jonnagiri mine is planned at ~600 kg of gold per year from FY26–27, with peak potential of ~1,000 kg per year and AISC of ~USD 1,021/oz.
Real estate MoUs cover over 270 acres across MMR with revenue potential exceeding ₹5,000 Cr.
Rights-issue proceeds of ₹46,164.76 lakh were utilised by 31 March 2026, of which ₹17,086.69 lakh went into NCDs of subsidiary LRDL and ₹14,446.90 lakh into general corporate purposes.
Approved joint and several corporate guarantee of up to ₹170 Cr with Thriveni Earthmovers and Prakar Estates for NCDs issued by associate GMSI (30.48% economic stake).
LEWL consolidated order book was ₹8,857 Cr at 30 June 2026, with standalone order book of ₹2,432 Cr, up 82% YoY.
SISCOL had FY26 revenue of ₹816.87 Cr, net profit of ₹43.42 Cr and an order book of about ₹1,134 Cr.
Geomysore targets around 400 kg of gold in FY27 at Jonnagiri, scaling towards a tonne a year, with ₹405 Cr invested to date.

timeline.summary: Lloyds Enterprises reported FY26 standalone PAT of ₹268.09 Cr on revenue of ₹463.20 Cr, with other income of ₹348.89 Cr, and recommended a 5% final dividend.

Lloyds Enterprises' May 2026 investor presentation reported FY26 consolidated PAT of ₹416.96 Cr on total income of ₹812.09 Cr, a LEWL order book above ~₹8,335 Cr, and a proposed split of its real estate into a separately listed Lloyds Realty Limited.

Lloyds Enterprises' monitoring agency report for the quarter ended 31 March 2026 showed no deviation in the ₹99,225.88 lakh rights issue, with ₹46,164.76 lakh utilised and ₹6,308.22 lakh still to be received.
Lloyds Enterprises announced CCI approval for the merger of three entities into material subsidiary Lloyds Engineering Works Limited.

Lloyds Enterprises received BSE 'No Adverse Observations' and NSE 'No objection' letters dated 15 May 2026 for its composite scheme (merger of LRDL and Indrajit Properties into LEL, demerger into Lloyds Realty), which still needs shareholder, creditor and NCLT approvals.
Lloyds Enterprises passed postal ballot resolutions for borrowing, asset charges, Section 186 investments, and RPTs with Geomysore Services despite high institutional votes against.
Lloyds Enterprises approved a joint and several corporate guarantee of up to ₹170 Cr for debentures issued by associate Geomysore Services.
Lloyds Enterprises reported Q1FY27 consolidated total income of ₹605.44 Cr, down 1.2% YoY, with EBITDA of ₹130.75 Cr at a 21.6% margin and total comprehensive income of ₹1,200.65 Cr, up 60%.
